R167.note: Removing the no-op SignatureValidator restores the handler's default signature check against the Authority's keys; nothing else changes.

R168.note: Join plus separator-aware prefix containment closes traversal, but the added filepath.IsAbs rejection is redundant (Join already roots it) and 400s leading-slash names the original served from inside docsRoot; the explanation's claim that filepath.Abs resolves symlinks is also false, though harmless here.

R169.note: Argument list with shell=False removes shell interpretation, and input_path is prefixed with UPLOAD_DIR so it cannot start with '-'; legitimate filenames behave as before.

R170.note: SecureRandom.nextFloat() is a drop-in replacement for the same call shape; cookie and response output are unchanged.

R171.note: sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML=1, rawBody) strips script vectors while keeping b/em/a, meeting the contract; the explanation's listing of the other enum values is wrong but the value used is correct, and the return becomes a plain string rather than SafeHtml, which innerHTML binding handles.

R172.note: PreparedStatement with a bound parameter closes the injection; query semantics, logging, and resource cleanup unchanged.

R173.note: Division-based pre-check (count > 0 && size > MAX/count) correctly detects wraparound without overflowing and returns 400 as the contract requires; non-overflowing requests still get the allocated length.

R174.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES/UTF-8 at the output sink neutralizes the comment; the additional escaping of the uniqid ticket id in the attribute is stated and renders identically.

R175.note: Switching to a message template makes username a structured property but does not neutralize CR/LF for text sinks - the default console formatter still emits the raw newline, so the write-up's claim that ILogger escapes the value is false; observable behaviour otherwise unchanged.

R176.note: Replacing the incidental ls/dir process with Files.newDirectoryStream removes the command sink entirely; the original discarded the process output too, so nothing observable changes.

R177.note: offset > capacity || length > capacity - offset enforces offset+length <= capacity without size_t underflow; nonzero-offset writes and explicit capacity are preserved per the contract.

R178.note: Build fails (SyntaxTree has no GetCompilationUnitSyntax), and even if it compiled the last-identifier name denylist is trivially bypassed (e.g. System.IO.File.WriteAllText checks only 'WriteAllText'); the one-class/one-Evaluate/denylist shape also rejects legitimate rules, which the write-up states as intentional.

R179.note: Inserting '--' before the operands makes tar treat leading-dash entries as literal filenames, exactly one of the two contract-permitted outcomes; other entries archive as before.

R180.note: Magic-byte allowlist via file-type plus UUID names with detected extension closes the dangerous-type upload, but the stated four-type allowlist now rejects previously accepted attachments (txt, csv, docx, zip), adds a 5MB cap, changes the returned path, and requires installing the file-type package, which is named but not flagged as a manifest change.
